blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: IRDAI was constituted as an autonomous statutory body under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999.
Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999 specifies the duties, powers, and functions of the Authority to regulate and promote orderly growth in insurance.
The primary mandate of IRDAI is protecting the interests of policyholders regarding claim settlements, surrender values, and terms of insurance contracts.
IRDAI regulates and registers insurance companies, reinsurance businesses, and intermediaries like brokers, agents, and loss assessors.
It specifies the required solvency margin that insurers must maintain at all times to ensure financial stability and claim settlement capability.

blocks.content: The primary duty of the Authority is to regulate, promote, and ensure orderly growth of the insurance business and re-insurance business in India while protecting the financial interests of policyholders.

items: IRDAI was established following the key recommendations of the Malhotra Committee Report (1994).
Headquarters was relocated from New Delhi to Hyderabad, Telangana in the year 2001.
The Authority comprises a 10-member composition: 1 Chairman, 5 full-time members, and 4 part-time members appointed by the Government of India.
Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999 defines the statutory powers, functions, and duties of IRDAI.
